definition: The depth of soil that a land-cover class's roots can draw water from, in InVEST Annual Water Yield. The model uses min(root_depth, soil depth) as the plant-available water column, so root_depth only bites where it is shallower than the soil. Commonly set to either the maximum rooting depth of the vegetation type, or the depth containing ~95% of root biomass (D95).
notes_on_convention: The InVEST User Guide describes root_depth as 'the maximum root depth for vegetated land use classes ... often given as the depth at which 95% of root biomass occurs.' Two defensible fillings: (a) maximum rooting depth from Canadell et al. (1996) - larger, used by many published InVEST AWY studies; (b) D95 from Schenk & Jackson (2002) - the 95%-biomass depth, closer to the UG wording and usually the better hydrological choice because the deepest 5% of roots contribute little transpiration. Pick one convention and apply it consistently. Non-vegetated classes (bare, built, water): set a small nominal value (e.g. 1-30 mm) or per the UG.

how_to_estimate.summary: Look up by biome and growth form. Prefer a regional root-profile study if one exists for your ecosystem. Then cap at the local soil / regolith depth (see fetch_soil variable=depth_to_bedrock).

methods.name: maximum rooting depth by biome/form
methods.notes: 290 obs, 253 species, 11 biomes. Global mean 4.6 m.

methods.name: D95 (95%-biomass depth) by biome
methods.notes: 475 profiles. Global ~2.0 m; ~0.4/0.7/1.1 m hold 80/90/95% of roots globally.

methods.name: cumulative-root-fraction model
methods.notes: beta model: cumulative root fraction = 1 - beta^depth_cm; solve for the depth at your target fraction per biome.

methods.name: FAO-56 effective rooting depth (crops)
methods.notes: cereals 1.0-1.8 m, maize 1.0-1.7 m, pasture 0.5-1.5 m, vegetables 0.3-1.0 m, deciduous orchard 1.0-2.0 m, vines 1.0-2.0 m.

how_to_choose: Match by growth form first (tree > shrub > herbaceous), then biome/water regime (water-limited woody systems root far deeper than mesic or cold ones). If your AWY run is sensitive to root_depth, it usually means soils are deep enough that root_depth is the binding constraint - then the convention choice (max vs D95) matters and should be stated. Where soils are shallow, any reasonable value > soil depth gives the same result.

context.study_area: Canadell et al. 1996 Table; Schenk & Jackson 2002

records.caveats: Individual maxima to 18 m; D95 much shallower. Usually soil/regolith depth limits this in practice.
records.provenance: standard reference (added; not in FS28 masterfile)

context.region: global synthesis (deep records from central Kalahari)

records.caveats: The 15 m biome mean is driven by a few extreme phreatophytes (Boscia albitrunca to 68 m). For hydrology use the D95 (~3-5 m), not the maximum.
Applies to much Australian mallee / dry sclerophyll scrub. Deep roots exploit stored soil water through the dry season.
Reasonable default for Pinus radiata plantation on deep soils.

context.region: global synthesis (eucalypt maxima from Australia are deeper)

records.caveats: SE Australian eucalypt forest can root well past 2.9 m where regolith allows (records to 10-40 m for some species); soil depth normally governs in AWY.

context.study_area: Canadell et al. 1996; herbaceous growth-form mean 2.6 m

records.caveats: Deep-rooted perennial C3/C4 grasses. Annual exotic pasture and heavily grazed swards are shallower (500-1000 mm).
FAO-56 'effective' rooting depth (where most water uptake occurs): wheat/barley 1.0-1.8 m, maize 1.0-1.7 m, soybean 0.6-1.3 m, vegetables 0.3-1.0 m. Use the mid value unless you know the crop.
Vegetables shallow (0.3-1.0 m), deciduous orchard and vines deeper (1.0-2.0 m), irrigated pasture 0.5-1.5 m. Irrigation often keeps effective uptake shallow regardless of potential depth.

context.study_area: Canadell et al. 1996 (boreal forest mean 2.0 m); tundra species from 0.3 m

records.caveats: A tiny non-zero value. Some workflows use 30 mm bare-soil evaporation depth. These classes usually also have LULC_veg = 0, so AWY uses the non-vegetated ET path anyway.
